title: Compute a value with an expression
description: Write a query that returns each product's `name` and its price after a 10% discount, labeled `discounted_price`, rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: expressions in SELECT
A SELECT list can contain computed expressions, not just column names - price * 0.9 computes a new value per row, the same way a column reference does.
Select name and ROUND(price * 0.9, 2) AS discounted_price from products.
expected_behavior: Returns each product's name and its price reduced by 10%, rounded to 2 decimals.
solution: SELECT name, ROUND(price * 0.9, 2) AS discounted_price FROM products;
explanation: SELECT doesn't require every item to be an existing column - price * 0.9 is evaluated per row exactly like a column would be, and ROUND() then formats that computed value.
postgres_note: ROUND(numeric, int) works directly on NUMERIC columns like price here; rounding a double precision value needs an explicit cast in PostgreSQL (ROUND(value::numeric, 2)).
